newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Fossil Fuel Levy upped to 0.7 pct Apr 97.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Fossil Fuel Levy upped to 0.7 pct Apr 97.

text.p: A levy on fossil fuel in Scotland will be increased by 0.2 percent to 0.7 percent from April 1, 1997, said Britain's electricity industry regulator, Stephen Littlechild.
The levy for England and Wales has already been set at 2.2 percent for 1997/98.

The Fossil Fuel Levy is required by law to recover the additional costs to Scottish Power Plc and Hydro-Electric of the Scottish Renewables Obligation (SRO), a Government initiative to support renewable energy generating capacity.
Under SRO, Scottish Power and Hydro-Electric are required to buy certain amounts of electricity capacity from renewable energy sources which include wind, hydro and waste generation.
The Levy applies to electricity generated from fossil fuel sources, such as coal, oil and gas, as well as to renewable energy sources under the SRO.
The Levy's impact on electricity users will be minimal.
"I estimate that the rate to apply in 1997/98 will increase the amount paid by the typical domestic customer, in respect of the levy, by about one stg per annum," Littlechild said in a statement.
